question: At which GA chord-symbol boundary should unsupported or ambiguous notation become an explicit result instead of a plausible but wrong chord?
hypothesis: GA's tolerant chord-symbol parser accepts unknown or partially interpreted suffixes, allowing a user-visible voicing response to carry an invented musical meaning. A small corpus and explicit parse outcomes can expose the boundary before changing the public API.
evidence: GA Common/GA.Domain.Services/Chords/Parsing/ChordSymbolParser.cs matches a valid root followed by any suffix, maps unrecognized suffixes to Major, and uses substring checks for alterations. Its TryParse catches every exception and returns only a boolean.

GA Tests/Common/GA.Business.Core.Tests/Chords/ChordSymbolParserTests.cs asserts only non-null/root/symbol on accepted cases and does not test an unknown suffix; C/E is listed as valid without a bass assertion.

GA Common/GA.Domain.Core/Theory/Harmony/Chord.cs has a separate TryFromSymbol path that rejects an unknown suffix but supports fewer chord forms; Chord.Bass is Notes[0], not parsed slash-bass metadata.

GA Apps/ga-server/GaApi/Services/VoicingFilterService.cs uses ChordSymbolParser.TryParse; Apps/ga-server/GaApi/Controllers/ContextualChordsController.cs returns 400 for ArgumentException and 200 for successfully parsed voicings.
state/streeling/fixtures/computer-science/cs-003/chord-symbol-corpus.json records source-traced predictions and desired outcomes; runtime regression and subject review are pending.
